title: New AI regulation may be needed to impede cyber risks, IMF official says
key_facts: Dan Katz, the International Monetary Fund's first deputy managing director, said new artificial-intelligence regulation may be needed to rein in development of cutting-edge tools that pose risks to society.
Katz said the leading risk is cybersecurity.
He said defenders will need to respond with the same frontier AI tools used by cyber actors.
He framed the wider question as whether increasingly powerful AI systems could pose such severe risks to society that new regulation is needed to slow the pace of development.
quote_evidence: New artificial-intelligence regulation may be needed to rein in development of cutting-edge tools that pose risks to society, said Dan Katz, the International Monetary Fund's first deputy managing director.
The leading risk is cybersecurity, he said, and defenders will need to respond with the same frontier AI tools used by cyber actors.
why_it_matters_hint: A top IMF official is saying that new rules on advanced AI may be needed, with cyber attacks as the main worry.
